model: Regulated utility free cash flow to equity capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; rate-base equity compounding, net debt zero)

inputs.share_count_basis: 662.88m shares outstanding (Q3-2026 10-Q cover) + 1.2m restricted stock + 3.8m treasury-method dilution from the 24.86m-share forward sale agreements (forward price ~$34.83 = $866m / 24.865m shares, against the current quote). Held FLAT in the engine: all later issuance (the forward's $866m and the modelled ATM sales) is charged as a negative equity flow inside 'capex', so growing the divisor as well would count it twice. The $650m 2.875% convertible notes due 2029 convert at $53.61 with principal settled in cash -- out of the money, no dilution included. The 4.25% 2026 convertibles were settled in August 2026 ($1.0bn cash + 4.12m shares, already in the count).
inputs.net_debt_note: Zero BY DESIGN: the flow is free cash flow to EQUITY (after interest), discounted at the cost of equity. Deducting debt again would double-count it. Actual debt is in total_debt_actual.
inputs.total_debt_actual_note: FY2025 10-K total debt per Metrics.csv (22,476 at Q1-2026); cash 132 at 2026-09-30 (128 of it in securitization VIEs). Memo only -- the engine fields total_debt/cash are zeroed with net_debt so the bridge does not deduct debt from an equity flow.
inputs.last_fcf_basis: FY2025 free cash flow to equity = dividends paid on common 574 less common stock issued 0 (FY2025 10-K cash flow statement). Not owner FCF: on this route the base flow is the cash that actually reached common holders.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K LTIP compensation expense $48m (FY2024 $34m, FY2023 $65m). Already expensed inside net income (GAAP and non-GAAP), so the forward SBC path is 0% to avoid charging it twice; house and street bases coincide.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T21:00:02Z regular close (Friday); no after-hours print involved
inputs.wacc_rationale: The discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is to equity. USD build: 10-year UST ~4.9% (the level recorded in this folder's AEE build a week earlier; not re-fetched) + regulated-utility equity beta ~0.65-0.7 x 4.6% ERP = ~8.0%. Set at the top of the 7.5-8.0% range used for AEE/AEP/AWK because CNP's earnings are concentrated in one Gulf Coast T&D franchise with hurricane exposure and holding-company leverage. Same rate in all three scenarios -- risk is carried by the scenario paths and weights, not by per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases (mainly TEEEF units, being released) are recovered in rates and sit inside O&M / interest, i.e. already inside pre-tax income. No separate lease line; lease path 0%.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material noncontrolling interest and no preferred stock outstanding; net income is wholly attributable to common.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. The dcf-methods routing table has no regulated-utility row. The operating-company row would send CNP to the unlevered owner-FCF DCF, which is unusable here: reported FCF is negative in every year since FY2019 (FY2021-25: -3,142 / -2,609 / -524 / -2,374 / -2,384; 9M-2026 OCF 2,051 vs capex 4,170) because growth capex under the $70.7bn 2026-2035 plan runs ~2x operating cash flow BY DESIGN and earns an allowed return once in rate base. SKILL.md says not to read structurally negative FCF as a signal, and the AIA.NZ precedent shows the firm-level DCF returns a meaningless number for a capex-supercycle regulated asset. Following the skill's principle (discount the flow the business actually produces, at the rate appropriate to whom it accrues) and this folder's AEE / AEP / AWK precedent, CNP is valued as a compounder of regulated book: FCFE = net income - increase in shareholders' equity = dividends - common stock issued, capitalised at the cost of equity with net debt held at zero, run through the Drivers engine. ENGINE MAPPING (read the sliders this way): 'revenue' = total revenues; 'EBITDA margin' = PRE-TAX income to common as % of revenue (after interest); 'cash tax' = GAAP effective rate, so 'NOPAT' = net income; D&A, SBC, lease = 0 (all inside pre-tax income); 'capex' = equity retained + common stock issued; 'FCF' = FCFE. EARNINGS BASIS: management's non-GAAP EPS (guidance basis), which excludes ZENS / equity-securities mark-to-market and divestiture effects; 9M-2026 GAAP diluted EPS is 1.34 and Q3 GAAP 0.50 vs non-GAAP 0.53, so the two are close and the excluded items are not recurring operating costs. The Q4-2026 gain/loss and tax on the Ohio LDC sale ($2.62bn: $1.42bn cash + $1.2bn 364-day seller note, closed 2026-10-01) is outside the model's earnings; the proceeds are debt/equity-plan funding, reflected through lower assumed issuance, not as a separate bridge item. Y1 = FY2026, three quarters reported. DATA GAP: Metrics.csv stops at Q1-2026; Q2/Q3-2026 figures here were read directly from the Q3-2026 10-Q text (income statement, cash flow, EPS and equity notes). CAVEATS: (1) the post-2027 equity issuance amounts are judgment -- the filings disclose only the $866m forward, a $1bn ATM (unused, none planned for 2026) and the capital plan; (2) no investor-presentation text was available, so rate-base and FFO/debt targets were not checked directly; consolidated ROE (~11% in FY2026E on average equity) is used as the consistency anchor instead; (3) house and street bases coincide (SBC inside net income), so band_position is not meaningful and should be read as collapsed.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR (6.0%) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue 3-yr (0.1%) and GAAP EPS 3-yr (0.2%). Revenue is distorted by gas-cost pass-through deflation and the Louisiana/Mississippi LDC sale; GAAP EPS by ZENS marks and divestiture items (FY2022 1.59 included gains). Neither is a usable growth anchor; forward growth is taken from guidance (7-9% non-GAAP EPS) cross-checked against the equity roll-forward at a constant ~11% ROE.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue FY2020 7,418 / FY2022 9,327 / FY2025 9,357. GAAP diluted EPS FY2022 1.59 / FY2025 1.60; FY2020 was -1.79 (Enable impairment), so a 5-yr EPS CAGR is undefined. Shareholders' equity FY2020 8,348 / FY2022 10,042 / FY2025 11,153. Firm-level FCF (OCF - capex) is negative in every year of both windows, so FCF CAGRs are null rather than a spurious figure -- the capex-supercycle signature, not distress. FCFE (dividends less issuance) was 574 in FY2025, 28 in FY2024 (522 dividends - 494 issued) and 485 in FY2023.

base.growth_note: Total revenue (a carrier line only; value is set by the net-income and equity paths the margin and 'capex' lines are back-solved from). FY2026: 9M-2026 revenue 7,318 vs 6,852 (+6.8%) less Q4 without the Ohio LDC (sold 2026-10-01). FY2027: remaining Ohio revenue and the ~$112m TEEEF rate reduction drop out against ~8% underlying growth. Thereafter tracks rate-base growth less pass-through drag, fading as the 10-year plan matures.
base.capex_note: NOT capex: equity retained plus common stock issued (increase in shareholders' equity invested in rate base) as % of revenue. Common stock issued $m [165, 866, 400, 500, 500, 300, 300, 200, 0, 0] (FY2026 = 165 actual forward settlement; FY2027 = 866 physical settlement of the 24.86m-share May-2025 forwards due by 2027-02-25; later years are a judgment, not guidance, issued at 18x that year's EPS). Dividend payout [0.49, 0.49, 0.49, 0.49, 0.49, 0.49, 0.5, 0.52, 0.6, 0.73] -> dividends [621, 699, 764, 838, 919, 994, 1089, 1208, 1474, 1875]. FCFE = dividends - issuance = [456, -167, 364, 338, 419, 694, 789, 1008, 1474, 1875]. Year-end equity [11964, 13558, 14753, 16125, 17581, 18916, 20305, 21621, 22604, 23297].
base.tax_note: GAAP effective rate, flat 20% (9M-2026 20.4% = 228/1,119; 9M-2025 14.1% was flattered by a state deferred-tax remeasurement). Cash tax is a net refund (9M-2026 refunds 90; CAMT refund claims under Treasury Notice 2026-7) but for a rate-regulated utility deferred-tax benefits flow back to customers through rate base, so the book rate is the economically right charge.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 8.0% cost of equity / 3.0% growth = 20.6x year-10 FCFE, which binds below the 24x cap; times the year-10 payout of 73% that is 15.0x year-10 earnings versus ~20x forward today, i.e. the model assumes a de-rating to the sector's long-run range. Year-10 payout is set to 1 - g/ROE so the terminal growth is self-funding with no further issuance.
base.narrative: Management delivers the midpoint: non-GAAP EPS $1.91 (FY2026 guide $1.90-1.92) and $2.08 (FY2027 guide $2.07-2.09), then 8%/yr to 2030 (the middle of the 7-9% target that management says it is tracking toward the upper half of), fading to 4.5% by 2035 as the $70.7bn plan matures. Houston Electric large-load connections arrive roughly on the ERCOT Batch Zero schedule, trackers recover ~85% of capex without material lag, and consolidated ROE holds at ~11% (the FY2026 level). Equity: the $866m forward settles in early 2027 and a further ~$2.2bn is issued 2028-2033 through the $1bn ATM and successors. Dividend grows with EPS at a ~49% payout until issuance stops, then payout rises to 73% as growth slows to the 3.0% terminal rate.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: roughly half of earnings sit under one regulator (PUCT) in one hurricane-exposed territory, the Analysis JSON rates leverage, interest-rate and regulatory-lag risk 'high', and the plan depends on continuous capital-market access. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: the base already takes management's guidance midpoint on a plan raised three times in 13 months, and the bull needs load growth, constructive regulation and low equity needs to coincide. Base 50%: guidance has been met or raised consistently and ~85% of capex is tracker- or forward-test-year-recoverable.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A regulated utility is a compounder of book: it earns an allowed return on equity invested in rate base and its value is the cash it can pay out after funding that growth. CNP is valued on FCFE (dividends less new equity) at an 8% cost of equity over ten years, with a Gordon terminal value at a payout that makes terminal growth self-funding. The result prices CNP at roughly 15x year-10 earnings; the market's ~20x forward multiple implies a cost of equity nearer 7%, so the gap to the quote is mostly a discount-rate disagreement, not a growth one.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount rate: each 0.5pt of cost of equity moves value by roughly 10%; the market is capitalising CNP at ~7%, the model at 8%.
Equity issuance after 2027 is modelled, not guided; every extra $1bn issued costs roughly $1/share in present value.
Consolidated ROE is held at ~11% in the base; one point of sustained ROE erosion (regulatory lag, storm-cost disallowance) removes ~9% of earnings.
Houston large-load demand (~12 GW in queue) may attrite; much of the plan above $65bn is sized on it.
Gulf Coast hurricane risk and contested recovery (TEEEF/Beryl ~$800m).
ZENS indexed debt: early exchange or redemption before 2029 would trigger a large cash tax payment not in the model.
Q4-2026 Ohio sale accounting and the $1.2bn seller note (credit exposure to National Fuel Gas) are outside the modelled earnings.
